source_policy.allowed_sources: Current 2026-2027 official college catalog program, linked option-menu, catalog-identity, and graduation-policy pages only.
source_policy.schedule_rule: Where a program page includes both categorical requirements and a suggested schedule, only the categorical requirements are composed. Central Virginia's four-term pathway is retained and reorganized because it is the current catalog's only course-requirement list; its term placement is not a degree rule.
source_policy.option_rule: A named catalog option source is walked to concrete courses. Multiple options are OR alternatives; a two-course science or calculus sequence is an AND route; cross-slot distinctness and no-double-count rules remain explicit constraints.
source_policy.arithmetic_rule: Catalog credit conflicts and variable-credit ranges remain visible. No unprinted filler course is invented; a residual units_fill is used only where the catalog itself directs students to select enough applicable elective credit to reach the award minimum.

findings: Central Virginia publishes a current 60-61 credit Computer Science A.S. under academic plan 246 and links three concrete UCGS option records.

Germanna publishes a current Computer Science A.S. plan 246 with a 60-credit minimum, an explicit 60-62 completion range, categorical degree requirements, UCGS options, and a separate approved transfer-elective dictionary.
Laurel Ridge publishes a current 60-64 credit Computer Science A.S. plan 246 with a complete categorical requirement list before a separately labeled suggested schedule.
All three current graduation policies require at least a 2.0 applicable-curriculum GPA and at least 25 percent institutional credit.

requirement_findings.introductory_science_slots: Two distinct four-credit slots, each with PHY 241 or CHM 111 as the exact menu.
requirement_findings.second_science_slot: One four-credit PHY 242 or CHM 112 choice; no same-discipline alignment statement is printed.
requirement_findings.block_ii: Two three-credit courses from different Art, Humanities, or Literature categories; 16 concrete options.
requirement_findings.block_iii: One three-credit Social and Behavioral Sciences course; 7 concrete options.
requirement_findings.block_vi: One three-credit History course; 5 concrete options.
requirement_findings.credit_variation: MTH 245 is three credits and MTH 264 is four credits in a row printed as four, producing the 60-61 range.

requirement_findings.transfer_electives: The categorical requirement prints 7-10 credits and directs students to choose enough approved coursework to reach 60-62 total credits.
requirement_findings.arts_humanities_literature: Two courses from two different categories; 25 concrete options.
requirement_findings.world_language_resolution: The generic world-language options are resolved to all 40 current concrete language-course codes in the official transfer-elective record.
requirement_findings.cross_requirement_conditions: CSC 205 is an elective only when not used for the major; MTH 265 and several GE options also appear in more than one menu and cannot be double counted.

requirement_findings.natural_science: Required CHM 111 and CHM 112 eight-credit AND sequence.
requirement_findings.mathematics: Required MTH 263 and MTH 264 eight-credit AND sequence.
requirement_findings.electives: Exactly two courses totaling 5-8 credits from 14 concrete options, including variable-credit CSC 295 and CSC 298.
requirement_findings.source_conflict: The fixed 55 credits plus the printed 5-8 elective range model 60-63, while the same page publishes 60-64.
